# `silk/compress/zip`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read the files and directories of a ZIP archive held in memory.

## When to use
Use a [`ZipReader`](#ZipReader) to unpack a `.zip` download, such as a vendor SDK or a release archive. Open
the archive with [`ZipReader.open`](#ZipReader.impl.open), call [`ZipReader.next`](#ZipReader.impl.next) until it returns none, and decode
each file with [`ZipMember.content`](#ZipMember.impl.content). This module does not write archives.

## Details
The reader walks the central directory at the end of the archive, so it accepts archives with a
trailing comment, data descriptors, extra fields, and ZIP64 sizes and offsets. Each member must
be stored or DEFLATE-compressed, unencrypted, and on one disk. A member's local header must agree
with its central record on method and name, and its data must lie before the central directory.
Names are checked before a member is returned: an absolute name, a backslash, a colon, a NUL, an
empty segment, or a `.` or `..` segment refuses the archive, so a caller that joins a name to a
directory and creates no symbolic links never writes outside it. A link's target is not checked,
so skip `SymbolicLink` members unless you check it. The reader does not detect repeated names.

[`ZipMember.content`](#ZipMember.impl.content) decodes one member and checks its length and CRC-32. The reader bounds the
sum of the decoded lengths that the central directory declares, so a caller can bound memory
before decoding anything.

## Errors
- [`ZipError`](#ZipError) from [`ZipReader.open`](#ZipReader.impl.open), [`ZipReader.next`](#ZipReader.impl.next), and [`ZipMember.content`](#ZipMember.impl.content) when the
  archive is malformed, uses a feature this module does not read, or goes over the limit.
- `OutOfMemoryError` from [`ZipMember.content`](#ZipMember.impl.content) if the `Allocator` fails.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.compress.zip {ZipError, ZipKind, ZipMember, ZipReader}
import silk.core.option {Option}
import silk.core.result {Result}

// Counts the regular files of `archive`, or answers -1 when it is not a valid ZIP archive.
fn files(archive: &[u8]) -> i32 {
  let mut reader = match ZipReader.open(archive, 1048576) {
    Result.Success {value} => move value
    Result.Failure {..} => { return -1 }
  }
  let mut count = 0
  while true {
    match ZipReader.next(&mut reader) {
      Result<Option<ZipMember>, ZipError>.Success {value} => match move value {
        Option<ZipMember>.Some {value: member} => { if member.kind == ZipKind.File { count = count + 1 } }
        Option<ZipMember>.None => { return count }
      }
      Result<Option<ZipMember>, ZipError>.Failure {..} => { return -1 }
    }
  }
  return count
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return files(b"PK\x05\x06\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00")
}
```

## `ZipError`

```silk
pub enum ZipError
```

The reason a ZIP archive was refused.

<a id="ZipError.Truncated"></a>

### `Truncated`

```silk
Truncated
```

A record runs past the end of the archive, or no end of central directory record is found.

<a id="ZipError.InvalidDirectory"></a>

### `InvalidDirectory`

```silk
InvalidDirectory
```

The end record, the central directory, or a local header is inconsistent: a bad signature, a
size or offset outside the archive, or a local header that disagrees with its central record.

<a id="ZipError.UnsupportedMember"></a>

### `UnsupportedMember`

```silk
UnsupportedMember
```

The archive spans disks, or a member is encrypted or uses a method other than stored or
DEFLATE.

<a id="ZipError.UnsafePath"></a>

### `UnsafePath`

```silk
UnsafePath
```

A member name is absolute, holds a backslash, a colon, or a NUL, or has an empty, `.`, or `..`
segment.

<a id="ZipError.InvalidData"></a>

### `InvalidData`

```silk
InvalidData
```

A member's data does not decode, or decodes to a length other than the one its record
declares.

<a id="ZipError.BadChecksum"></a>

### `BadChecksum`

```silk
BadChecksum
```

A member's decoded data does not match its CRC-32.

<a id="ZipError.LimitExceeded"></a>

### `LimitExceeded`

```silk
LimitExceeded
```

The decoded lengths the central directory declares go over the limit given to
[`ZipReader.open`](#ZipReader.impl.open).

<a id="ZipMember"></a>

## `ZipMember`

```silk
pub struct ZipMember<'a>
```

One member of a ZIP archive: its checked name and metadata, and its data still compressed.

### Details
The slices borrow the archive given to [`ZipReader.open`](#ZipReader.impl.open). `length` and `checksum` come from the
central directory, and [`ZipMember.content`](#ZipMember.impl.content) checks the decoded data against them.

<a id="ZipMember.name"></a>

### Field `name`

```silk
pub name: &'a [u8]
```

The member's path, with `/` between segments and no trailing `/`. The reader has refused
absolute paths and `..` segments.

<a id="ZipMember.kind"></a>

### Field `kind`

```silk
pub kind: ZipKind
```

Whether the member is a file, a directory, or a symbolic link.

<a id="ZipMember.executable"></a>


<a id="ZipReader"></a>

## `ZipReader`

```silk
pub struct ZipReader<'a>
```

A position in the central directory of a ZIP archive held in memory.

### When to use
Make one with [`ZipReader.open`](#ZipReader.impl.open) and call [`ZipReader.next`](#ZipReader.impl.next) until it returns none.

### Details
The reader does not allocate and borrows the archive. Each member it returns has passed the
name, bounds, and local header checks. After a failure, discard the reader.

<a id="ZipReader.impl"></a>

## Implementation `ZipReader<'a>`

```silk
impl<'a> ZipReader<'a>
```

<a id="ZipReader.impl.open"></a>

### Associated function `open`

```silk
pub fn open(archive: &'a [u8], maxDecodedBytes: u64) -> Result<ZipReader<'a>, ZipError>
```

Opens `archive` and checks its end records, allowing at most `maxDecodedBytes` of decoded
data across all members.

#### Errors
- [`ZipError`](#ZipError) with `Truncated` when no end of central directory record is found,
  `InvalidDirectory` when the end records point outside the archive, `UnsupportedMember` when
  the archive spans disks.

<a id="ZipReader.impl.next"></a>

### Method `next`

```silk
pub fn next(self: &mut ZipReader<'a>) -> Result<Option<ZipMember<'a>>, ZipError>
```

Returns the next member in central directory order, or none after the last.

#### Errors
- [`ZipError`](#ZipError) when the member's records are truncated or inconsistent, it is encrypted or
  uses an unsupported method, its name is unsafe, or its declared length goes over the limit.

<a id="ZipMember.impl.content"></a>

### Method `content`

```silk
pub effect fn content(self: &ZipMember<'a>) -> Bytes ! ZipError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the decoded data of `self`: a file's bytes, a link's target, or nothing for a
directory.

#### Errors
- [`ZipError`](#ZipError) with `InvalidData` when the data does not decode to exactly `length` bytes, or
  `BadChecksum` when its CRC-32 is not `checksum`.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.
